content: 1. Elagolix and Palovarotene: Elagolix reduces the levels or effects of palovarotene by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. It is recommended to avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. If coadministration is necessary, close monitoring is required. 2. Elagolix and Panobinostat: Elagolix decreases the levels of panobinostat by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is advised. Elagolix acts as a weak-to-moderate CYP3A4 inducer, so CYP3A substrates should be monitored if coadministered. Dose adjustments of CYP3A substrates may be necessary. 3. Elagolix and Pantoprazole: Elagolix increases the levels or effects of pantoprazole by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Elagolix is a weak CYP2C19 inhibitor, so caution is advised when using sensitive CYP2C19 substrates. 4. Elagolix and Paricalcitol: Elagolix reduces the levels of paricalcitol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. Elagolix is a weak-to-moderate CYP3A4 inducer, and CYP3A substrates should be monitored during coadministration. Dose adjustments of CYP3A substrates may be necessary. 5. Elagolix and Pazopanib: Pazopanib increases the levels or effects of elagolix through mechanisms involving P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Conversely, elagolix decreases pazopanib levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated, and close monitoring is essential if coadministration is unavoidable. 6. Elagolix and Pemigatinib: Elagolix decreases the levels or effects of pemigatinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Close monitoring is required if coadministration is necessary. 7. Elagolix and Pentamidine: Elagolix increases the levels or effects of pentamidine by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Elagolix is a weak CYP2C19 inhibitor, so caution is advised when using sensitive CYP2C19 substrates. 8. Elagolix and Pentobarbital: Pentobarbital decreases the levels or effects of elagolix by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution should be exercised, and close monitoring is required. 9. Elagolix and Perampanel: Elagolix reduces the levels of perampanel by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is necessary. Elagolix is a weak-to-moderate CYP3A4 inducer, and CYP3A substrates should be monitored during coadministration. Dose adjustments of CYP3A substrates may be required. 10. Elagolix and Pexidartinib: Elagolix decreases the levels of pexidartinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Elagolix is a weak-to-moderate CYP3A4 inducer, so CYP3A substrates should be monitored if coadministered. Dose adjustments of CYP3A substrates may be necessary. 11. Elagolix and Phenobarbital: Phenobarbital decreases the levels or effects of elagolix by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Conversely, elagolix increases the levels or effects of phenobarbital by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are advised. Elagolix is a weak CYP2C19 inhibitor. 12. Elagolix and Norethindrone Acetate: Phenobarbital decreases the levels or effects of norethindrone acetate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination should be avoided or replaced with an alternative drug. Hormonal contraceptives may not be reliable for effective birth control when coadministered, and there may be an increased incidence of menstruation-associated adverse effects such as amenorrhea, dysmenorrhea, or menorrhagia. Close monitoring is required. 13. Elagolix and Phenytoin: Phenytoin decreases the levels or effects of elagolix by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Conversely, elagolix increases the levels or effects of phenytoin by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Elagolix is a weak CYP2C19 inhibitor. 14. Elagolix and Progesterone Intravaginal Gel: Elagolix decreases the levels of progesterone intravaginal gel by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Elagolix is a weak-to-moderate CYP3A4 inducer, and CYP3A substrates should be monitored during coadministration. Dose adjustments of CYP3A substrates may be required. 15. Elagolix and Quinidine: Elagolix increases the levels or effects of quinidine by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Conversely, elagolix decreases quinidine levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Elagolix is a weak-to-moderate CYP3A4 inducer.
